finding: Split is spelling-blind and leak-free: TRAIN/HELD_OUT selection and allocation both key off stolfi_coordinate hashes, never voynich_token text, and no selected token string is duplicated across the 26-label sample.
evidence: freeze_split.py uses sample_rank_sha256/split_rank_sha256 keyed only on stolfi_coordinate; AUDIT SPLIT_LEAKAGE_TOKEN_DUPLICATES check: 26 selected, 26 distinct tokens, 0 duplicates.

finding: STAR and PLANET_MOON are pooled into a single TRAIN/HELD_OUT statistic, which hides that the two classes carry very unequal sample sizes (16 vs 4 TRAIN items) and cannot be judged against the same null. A class-conditioned null rerun for this audit (30 replicates/control) shows STAR (7/16=43.75%) sits only mildly above its own null mean (36-40%, pointwise p 0.20-0.40, not significant) and PLANET_MOON (3/4=75%) is squarely null-compatible once compared to its own n=4 null (under RANDOM_VOYNICH_SET, 73% of null replicates already meet or exceed 75%).
evidence: M1_AUDIT_DIAGNOSTICS.tsv PER_CLASS_BREAKDOWN rows (model_rank 1-10); M1_AUDIT_PERCLASS_NULL.tsv (30 reps/control, per-class coverage); pooled headline in M1_TOKEN_FORMATION_REPORT.md is 10/20=0.50.
impact: Interpretation risk: a reader could believe the pooled 50% reflects uniform partial support across the astronomical vocabulary, or (on a naive per-class split without a matching per-class null) that STAR underperforms and PLANET_MOON outperforms chance. Correctly null-conditioned, neither class shows a significant departure from chance individually -- consistent with, and arguably a stronger version of, the pooled NULL_COMPATIBLE verdict. Does not overturn the verdict, but changes what evidence it rests on and shows the pooled statistic cannot be naively decomposed.
required_fix: Report and threshold-gate STAR and PLANET_MOON coverage, HELD_OUT, and null comparisons separately in any future run, always against a class-conditioned null (not the pooled null and not a naive raw-percentage read) given the sample sizes are this unequal.

finding: The PLANET_MOON sample's uniqueness assumption (one label = one distinct historical planet, enforced by anonymous one-to-one matching) is itself uncertain: all 5 sampled PLANET_MOON labels come from the f67r2 "moon" diagram, where the underlying Stolfi/Zandbergen transcription comments describe them as a numbered sequence ("moon 1", "moon 3", "moon 4", "moon 6", "moon 9", "moon 11") with the annotator's own question-marked planetary guesses ("the Sun?", "Venus?", "Mercury?", "Saturn?", "Jupiter?", "Mars?"), not confirmed distinct planet names. Consistent with this being coincidence rather than signal, the specific object identity assigned to the same PLANET_MOON label is unstable across otherwise-equally-ranked model families: f67r2.L.1 is canonically matched to PLANET_IUPITER under one rule family (M1_001-M1_006) and to PLANET_VENUS under another (M1_007-M1_010), with f67r2.L.6 flipping between PLANET_LUNA and PLANET_IUPITER correspondingly.
evidence: research/stolfi_label_inventory/STOLFI_ASTRO_LABEL_MATCHES.tsv rows 0116-0129 (object_type=planet?, comment field); M1_LABEL_TERM_ASSIGNMENTS.tsv canonical_assignment=1 rows for object_class=PLANET_MOON across M1_001..M1_010 (identity flips between rule families despite constant 3/4 coverage).
impact: If this diagram in fact encodes a repeating/positional category (e.g. moon-phase or lunar-mansion count) rather than seven distinct named planets, the one-object-per-label matching model is the wrong model for this sub-class regardless of which transformation rule is tested, independent of coverage numbers. The identity instability across rule families further suggests the 3/4 match count reflects the model class's freedom rather than a stable underlying correspondence.
required_fix: Before weighting PLANET_MOON results (including in any dictionary-expansion follow-up), add an explicit methodological note on the uniqueness assumption for this specific diagram, or treat PLANET_MOON results as advisory-only until independently corroborated.

finding: Dictionary capacity is not the limiting factor for either class, even in the worst case. STAR has 21 historical objects for 21 sampled labels (16 TRAIN + 5 HELD_OUT); because a matching never uses more objects than TRAIN labels (<=16), at least 21-16=5 objects always remain for the 5 HELD_OUT labels regardless of which 16 are chosen. PLANET_MOON has 7 objects for 5 labels (2 slack).
evidence: M1_AUDIT_DIAGNOSTICS.tsv DICTIONARY_CAPACITY_CEILING rows: STAR joint_ceiling_pct=100.0, worst_case_held_ceiling_if_train_saturates=5 (=held_labels); PLANET_MOON joint_ceiling_pct=100.0, worst_case_held_ceiling=1 (=held_labels).
impact: None — the deliberate design choice (STAR sample size = STAR dictionary size, documented in TOKEN_FORMATION_RULE_SPACE.md) achieves its stated purpose of preventing capacity from artificially capping coverage.

finding: Anonymous one-to-one matching is implemented correctly: one object cannot serve two labels, documented spelling variants are alternative attestations of the same object (not additional objects), and HELD_OUT exclusion is scoped to only the objects the canonical TRAIN maximum matching actually used. Every unexplained label in the retained models fails with reason NO_COMPLETE_MAPPED_TERM (zero compatible candidates), never a one-to-one assignment conflict.
evidence: Code reading of preprocess()/maximum_matching()/compute_heldout(); M1_UNEXPLAINED_LABELS.tsv: 432/432 rows reason_unmatched=NO_COMPLETE_MAPPED_TERM, 0 rows ONE_TO_ONE_ASSIGNMENT_CONFLICT.
impact: Confirms the a-priori concern that object-disjoint HELD_OUT could "artificially" starve HELD_OUT of feasible objects (raised in the task brief) does not materialize in this run: the observed 0/6 HELD_OUT is a genuine no-candidate result, not a matching-contention artifact.

finding: Matching ambiguity/degeneracy is empirically negligible in the retained models despite the substitution table's large nominal degrees of freedom: the top-ranked model (M1_001) has assignment_multiplicity=1 and ambiguity_excess=0.0 (every matched label has exactly one compatible object); across the top 25 retained models ambiguity_excess never exceeds 0.05.
impact: The theoretical risk of "artificial gain from interchangeable objects" (Section 3) is real in principle for this model class but not realized in the actual retained models, because the 1-or-2-unit length/segmentation constraint prunes most spurious candidate pairs before matching runs.

finding: The target EVA composite inventory (cth, ckh, cph, cfh, iin, ain, ch, sh, ee, in) is a repository-wide frozen convention used in an earlier, independent experiment (research/astro_label_cross_section/main.py), not chosen or tuned specifically for the M1 astronomical-label search.
evidence: grep across repo: TARGET_COMPOSITES/equivalent list appears identically in research/astro_label_cross_section/main.py, research/astro_token_formation/main.py, and research/astro_token_formation_m1/main.py.
impact: Rules out a specific overfitting risk (segmentation reverse-engineered from this label set to maximize matches).

finding: M1's abbreviation step (SUSPEND_1/SUSPEND_2/PREFIX_3/PREFIX_4) truncates by segmented-unit count (len(units), where a digraph like "kh" counts as one unit), while M0's original rule of the same name truncates by raw character count (len(value)). M1 reuses M0's Rule.complexity cost for these labels unchanged, so identical complexity costs can correspond to measurably different amounts of information discarded whenever a source form contains a digraph before the truncation point.
evidence: research/astro_token_formation_m1/main.py abbreviate() (operates on units) vs research/astro_token_formation/main.py apply_rule() abbreviation block (operates on value, a string) — M1_SUBSTITUTION_RULE_SPACE.md acknowledges the reinterpretation ("This is exactly computable by selecting those source units before substitution") but the complexity accounting was not re-derived for it.
impact: Narrow-impact (only affects source forms containing a SOURCE_DIGRAPHS sequence near the truncation boundary), but means total_complexity is not strictly comparable in information-theoretic terms to M0's complexity for pipelines using these four abbreviation modes.
required_fix: Either re-derive an M1-specific abbreviation complexity cost, or document explicitly that the M0 complexity labels are reused only nominally (same rule name) and not as an exactly equivalent cost.

finding: M1's winning models use a substitution table that is close to an unconstrained monoalphabetic-with-two-unit-output cipher (18-19 of ~19 mapped source letters emit a freely chosen two-EVA-unit sequence drawn from ~20 possible target units, i.e. up to ~400 possible outputs per letter, constrained only by global self-consistency). This model class is expected to coincidentally satisfy roughly half of 20 short independent string-matching constraints regardless of the input's genuine content, which is exactly what all three null controls also achieve (max coverage 0.500 in every one of 300 replicates).
evidence: M1_MODEL_DETAILS/M1_001.md substitution table (18 of 19 entries are one_to_two); M1_NULL_RESULTS.tsv / M1_AUDIT_DIAGNOSTICS.tsv NULL_SUMMARY_CROSSCHECK (all three controls: max=0.500).
impact: Not a defect in the verdict (the frozen bands already classify this as NULL_COMPATIBLE/NO_MODEL, correctly), but the frozen report does not state explicitly that ~50% is close to the generic ceiling of this model class independent of input, which this audit's beam-width/order sweep and null cross-check now demonstrate directly.
required_fix: Add one sentence to any future M1-family report noting that a large, mostly-free one/two-unit substitution table is expected to reach roughly half coverage on ~20 short strings by construction, independent of genuine historical signal, so that readers do not need to infer this solely from the p-value.

finding: The frozen beam width (64) and the frozen label-visit order are not silently suppressing a materially better compact mapping. Sweeping beam width from 8 to 256 (4x the frozen width) reproduces TRAIN coverage 0.500 with mapping_size 19 at every width from 16 up. Sweeping label visit order (frozen edge-count-ascending vs. descending, coordinate-ascending, coordinate-descending) also converges to TRAIN coverage 0.500 in all four orderings, via different specific mappings (sizes 19/20/22/23) -- confirming genuine multiple local optima at the same ceiling, not one fragile solution, and confirming no order/width perturbation finds anything better than the frozen result.
evidence: M1_AUDIT_DIAGNOSTICS.tsv BEAM_WIDTH_SWEEP (widths 8/16/32/64/128/256, all best_train_coverage=0.5) and VISIT_ORDER_SWEEP (4 orderings, all best_train_coverage=0.5).
impact: Strengthens confidence in the NO_MODEL/NULL_COMPATIBLE verdict: it is robust to a 4x larger search budget and to the (somewhat arbitrary) visit-order tie-break, not an artifact of one specific bounded-search configuration.

finding: M1_MANIFEST.json's recorded input_sha256 for research/astro_token_formation_m1/main.py does not match either the currently committed file or the working tree copy (both identical to each other), meaning the manifest cannot by itself certify which exact script produced the frozen M1 artifacts.
evidence: python3 hash check: manifest hash 68a3102f...; git HEAD and working-tree hash 5eb7a764... (identical to each other, differ from manifest).
impact: Independent reproduction in this audit (rerunning the current script) reproduces M1_001 exactly byte-for-byte on the reported metrics, so the discrepancy appears to be a stale hash from a late, behavior-preserving edit rather than a result-affecting change -- but this cannot be proven from the manifest alone.
required_fix: Regenerate M1_MANIFEST.json/M1_SHA256SUMS from the current main.py before treating M1 as fully provenance-verified for any downstream comparison (e.g. a dictionary-expansion run).

finding: The three null controls (RANDOM_VOYNICH_SET, SHUFFLED_TERMS, PSEUDODICTIONARY) model distinct, non-redundant null hypotheses, each reruns the full 640-pipeline bounded optimiser per replicate (not a fixed-target comparison), and RANDOM_VOYNICH_SET draws from real observed Currier-A occurrences rather than synthetic random strings, which is the more conservative (harder-to-beat) choice.
evidence: See M1_AUDIT_NULL_REVIEW.md for the per-control invariant-preservation table and code-reading verification of null_worker/alter_terms/randomize_labels.
impact: None — the null design correctly accounts for the search's own multiple-comparisons freedom, which is the single most common way this kind of null design goes wrong.

finding: RANDOM_VOYNICH_SET does not condition the replacement Voynich token draw on the label's object_class, unlike the other two controls; this is inert in practice because matching is separately restricted by object_class downstream in build_edges(), but the report does not state this explicitly.
evidence: research/astro_token_formation_m1/main.py randomize_labels() (length-only pool) vs alter_terms() (class-conditioned alphabet); build_edges() term_class filter.
required_fix: Add a one-line note in the rule-space doc clarifying why class-conditioning is unnecessary for this specific control.

finding: Re-scoring the top 10 retained models' frozen mappings against HELD_OUT under a FORM/RULE-DISJOINT semantics (objects not excluded after TRAIN use) produces the identical result (0/6) as the frozen OBJECT-DISJOINT semantics, for every one of the 10 models tested.
evidence: M1_AUDIT_DIAGNOSTICS.tsv HELDOUT_SEMANTICS_COMPARISON rows: object_disjoint_heldout_coverage == form_rule_disjoint_heldout_coverage == 0.0 for model_rank 1-10.
impact: Confirms the frozen HELD_OUT=0/6 result does not depend on which disjointness semantics is used -- it is not an artifact of the (defensible, since each STAR/PLANET label plausibly denotes a distinct object) object-disjoint choice. The choice between the two semantics remains conceptually important for interpretation (per F03) but did not change this run's outcome.
required_fix: None required for this run; still worth stating both semantics explicitly in any future report per Section 9 of the audit brief.

finding: The 20-item TRAIN sample gives 5%-wide discrete coverage levels (1/20 steps), which is reasonably fine-grained relative to the 70% gate, but the 6-item HELD_OUT sample gives only 16.7%-wide steps (1/6), so the frozen STRONG_CANDIDATE gate of HELD_OUT>=0.50 requires exactly 3/6 and cannot be approached gradually -- a single held-out item flips the gate by a full 16.7 percentage points.
impact: Not a design error given n=6 is essentially fixed by how many single-token, exactly-matched, spelling-blind-eligible PLANET_MOON/STAR labels exist at all -- but readers should not treat a HELD_OUT gate crossing (e.g. 3/6 vs 2/6) as more precise evidence than a 6-item binomial sample can support.
required_fix: State the discrete HELD_OUT resolution explicitly alongside the frozen 0.50 gate in any future report so the gate's precision is not overread.
